correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=2 and n>=1, the rearrangement inequality gives the exact support function as a weighted sum of positive sorted coordinate values. Gaussian radial independence determines the mean-width normalization using the expected chi radius. The order-statistic density gives the exact integral. A Gaussian quantile law, uniform Gaussian first-moment tails, and uniform L2 bounds justify the m->infinity expectation limit for every n/m->alpha>0 finite. Explicit quantile integrals give an affine limiting branch for alpha>=1/2, strict convexity below it, C2 matching, and a right-minus-left third-derivative jump 2sqrt(2pi). Exhaustive small instance and sampled numerical checks passed; no finite experiment is substituted for the analytical proof.

value.rationale: Euclidean mean width measures rotationally averaged support, a natural first-intrinsic-volume-type invariant of a well-studied discrete-polytopal family. The finite identity covers all dimensions and label budgets, including sparse and dense cases. Its limiting shape profile exhibits a precise half-density transition between budget-limited and positive-coordinate-limited support, with a sharp and nontrivial third-derivative discontinuity. This is a natural complete size-limit classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of volumes, Ehrhart data, or extremal radii.
